title: What is Gerrymandering? And Other Useful Political Terms!
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: To revise or alter the shape, layout, or design of something
The official process of modifying the boundaries of electoral districts.
A defined area whose residents vote for a representative in a parliament or congress.
A position of authority or representation in a parliament.
Borders or limits that define an area, region, or jurisdiction.
A person actively involved in government, typically holding or seeking elected office.

sentences.en: In today’s episode, I’m going to talk about a very interesting political topic, gerrymandering.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目里，我将聊聊一个非常有趣的政治话题——选区划界舞弊（gerrymandering）。

sentences.en: Gerrymandering is not just an interesting word, it is also a serious issue and especially relevant right now.
sentences.zh: Gerrymandering不仅是一个有趣的词，它也是一个严重的问题，而且与当下息息相关。

sentences.en: It is constantly in the news in the USA, as this year, Texas and some other US states have decided to redraw or change their congressional maps.
sentences.zh: 它在美国新闻中频频出现，因为今年得克萨斯州和美国其他一些州决定重新划分或更改他们的国会选区地图。

sentences.en: This is of course causing a lot of political tension and debate across the country and has brought the word gerrymandering back into people’s vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 这当然在全国范围内引起了大量的政治紧张局势和辩论，并让“gerrymandering”这个词重新回到了人们的词汇表中。

sentences.en: In this episode, I’m going to explain what gerrymandering is, why it happens, and whether it should be allowed.
sentences.zh: 在这期节目中，我将解释什么是gerrymandering、它为什么会发生，以及它是否应该被允许。

sentences.en: And then I want to also look at some other unusual English political words and phrases that I think you guys will all be interested in and maybe can add to your vocabulary in the future.
sentences.zh: 然后我还想介绍一些其他不常见的英语政治词汇和短语，我想你们大家都会感兴趣，也许以后还能丰富你们的词汇量。

sentences.en: Right now, gerrymandering is a big topic in the news because of events happening in Texas.
sentences.zh: 目前，由于得克萨斯州发生的事件，gerrymandering成为了新闻中的热门话题。

sentences.en: The Republican party in Texas is redrawing congressional maps, so the maps that are used to elect people to Congress in the USA.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州的共和党正在重新划分国会选区地图，也就是用于选举美国国会议员的地图。

sentences.en: This is very unusual because these maps are normally only changed after the census every 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这非常不寻常，因为这些地图通常只在每10年一次的人口普查之后才会更改。

sentences.en: The census is the national survey to discover how many people are living in a country, who they are and where they’re living.
sentences.zh: 人口普查是一项全国性调查，旨在查明一个国家有多少人口、他们是谁以及他们住在哪里。

sentences.en: This early redistricting is called mid-decade redistricting.
sentences.zh: 这种提前进行的选区重划被称为“十年中期选区重划”。

sentences.en: The main reason they are doing this is because of political advantage.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做的主要原因是出于政治利益。

sentences.en: The Republican party in Texas wants to gain more seats in Congress.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州的共和党希望在国会中获得更多席位。

sentences.en: They want to secure their power before the 2026 elections.
sentences.zh: 他们希望在2026年选举之前巩固自己的权力。

sentences.en: They are hoping to take advantage of recent trends in voting, such as Latino voters or Spanish speaking voters in Texas who tended to support the Republican Party in the 2024 Presidential election.
sentences.zh: 他们希望能利用近期的投票趋势，比如在2024年总统大选中倾向于支持共和党的得克萨斯州拉丁裔或西班牙语选民。

sentences.en: So by changing the boundaries of districts, they hope they can increase the number of Republican representatives in Congress, even if the overall vote is actually closer during the election.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过改变选区边界，他们希望能够增加国会中共和党代表的数量，即使在选举中总得票率其实非常接近。

sentences.en: They do this by changing the boundaries of districts to include more voters who support their party, the Republican Party, or to reduce the number of voters who support the opposition, the Democratic party.
sentences.zh: 他们通过改变选区边界来实现这一点，把更多支持他们党派（共和党）的选民划进来，或者减少支持反对党（民主党）的选民人数。

sentences.en: Imagine there are two electoral districts next to each other.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，有两个相邻的选举区。

sentences.en: One district voted 80% for the Republicans and 20% for the Democrats in the last election.
sentences.zh: 在最近的一次选举中，第一个选区有80%的人投给共和党，20%的人投给民主党。

sentences.en: The second district voted 45% for Republicans and 55% for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 第二个选区有45%的人投给共和党，55%的人投给民主党。

sentences.en: Each district elects just one politician.
sentences.zh: 每个选区只选出一名政治人物。

sentences.en: You could change these districts. Because they’re next to each other, you could redraw the map.
sentences.zh: 你可以改变这些选区。因为它们相邻，所以你可以重新绘制地图。

sentences.en: You could redraw the boundaries so that the second district has more Republican voters and less Democrat voters, while still keeping a big majority in the first district.
sentences.zh: 你可以重新划分边界，让第二个选区有更多的共和党选民和更少的民主党选民，同时在第一个选区仍然保持绝对优势。

sentences.en: In response to the Texas plans, some Democratic politicians left Texas to try and stop this redistricting.
sentences.zh: 为了回应得克萨斯州的计划，一些民主党政治人物离开得州，试图阻止这次选区重划。

sentences.en: This was a dramatic tactic, but it has been used before, including the last time mid-decade redistricting was attempted in 2003.
sentences.zh: 这是一个激进的策略，但以前也使用过，包括2003年上次尝试进行十年中期选区重划时。

sentences.en: This time, the Texas Governor Greg Abbott threatened to arrest legislators and politicians who tried to block the process.
sentences.zh: 这一次，得州州长Greg Abbott威胁要逮捕那些试图阻挠这一进程的议员和政治人物。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court has also influenced this situation.
sentences.zh: 最高法院也对这一局势产生了影响。

sentences.en: In 2019, the court said that federal courts, so national level courts in the USA, cannot stop gerrymandering or redistricting.
sentences.zh: 在2019年，法院表示联邦法院（即美国国家级法院）不能阻止gerrymandering或选区重划。

sentences.en: Which means that states have more freedom to draw maps in favor of one party.
sentences.zh: 这意味着各州有更大的自由度来画出有利于某一政党的地图。

sentences.en: However, the Voting Rights Act of 1965 still puts limits on reducing the voting power of minority groups, and there are lots of ongoing legal cases about this.
sentences.zh: 然而，1965年的《选举权法》仍然对削弱少数群体投票权的行为进行了限制，并且有许多关于此事的未决法律诉讼。

sentences.en: Other states are watching Texas closely.
sentences.zh: 其他州正在密切关注得克萨斯州。

sentences.en: New York, California, Missouri, Florida, and Ohio could see similar battles over redistricting, and this could definitely affect the balance of power in the US Congress, especially in the US House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 纽约州、加利福尼亚州、密苏里州、佛罗里达州和俄亥俄州可能会看到类似的选区重划之争，这绝对会影响美国国会尤其是美国众议院的权力平衡。

sentences.en: So in this episode, I’ve used the term gerrymandering a few times.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一期节目中，我已经用了好几次“gerrymandering”这个词。

sentences.en: I guess I should try and explain what gerrymandering is in more detail.
sentences.zh: 我想我应该试着更详细地解释一下什么是gerrymandering。

sentences.en: The word comes from Elbridge Gerry, a governor of Massachusetts in the US in the early 1800s.
sentences.zh: 这个词来源于Elbridge Gerry，他是19世纪初美国马萨诸塞州的一位州长。

sentences.en: He created an electoral district, shaped like a salamander to help his party win elections.
sentences.zh: 他创造了一个形状像蝾螈的选举区，来帮助他的政党赢得选举。

sentences.en: That combination of his name, Gerry, and the strange shape, Salamander, gave us the term gerrymander.
sentences.zh: 他的名字Gerry和那个奇怪的形状Salamander组合在一起，就成了gerrymander这个词。

sentences.en: So gerrymandering is when politicians draw or design voting districts to give their party an advantage.
sentences.zh: 所以gerrymandering是指政治人物为了让自己的政党占据优势而绘制或设计投票选区。

sentences.en: Instead of voters choosing politicians. Gerrymandering allows politicians to choose their voters by shaping districts.
sentences.zh: 与其说是选民选择政治人物，不如说是gerrymandering让政治人物通过塑造选区来选择他们的选民。

sentences.en: And these districts can often be very strange in shape.
sentences.zh: 而且这些选区的形状往往非常奇怪。

sentences.en: They might be very long and thin. Or in the case of Elbridge Gerry look like a salamander.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会又长又细。或者像Elbridge Gerry那样看起来像一只蝾螈。

sentences.en: There are two main techniques politicians use to gerrymander.
sentences.zh: 政治人物进行gerrymandering主要采用两种技术。

sentences.en: The first technique is called packing. This is when opposition voters are concentrated into a single district.
sentences.zh: 第一种技术被称为“打包”（packing）。这是指将反对派选民集中到一个单一的选区中。

sentences.en: By putting most or many of the opposition party supporters in one area, that district will obviously vote strongly for the opposition, but it reduces their influence in other districts.
sentences.zh: 通过把反对党的大多数或许多支持者放在一个区域，该选区显然会坚定地投票给反对派，但这却降低了他们在其他选区的影响力。

sentences.en: The second technique is called cracking.
sentences.zh: 第二种技术被称为“裂解”（cracking）。

sentences.en: This is when opposition voters are spread across several districts.
sentences.zh: 这是指将反对派选民分散到几个不同的选区中。

sentences.en: Their votes are diluted, made weak, so they are unlikely to have a majority in any district.
sentences.zh: 他们的选票被稀释、被削弱，因此他们在任何选区都不太可能占据多数。

sentences.en: This makes it easier for the party in power to win more districts, even if the overall vote is close.
sentences.zh: 这使得当权党更容易赢得更多选区的胜利，即使总得票率很接近。

sentences.en: So the two techniques again, are put all of your opposition voters in one district so that they don’t affect anywhere else in the State, or spread them around the State so that they’re not as powerful.
sentences.zh: 所以这两种技术再次说明，要么把所有的反对派选民都塞进一个选区，让他们影响不到州内其他地方；要么把他们分散到全州各地，让他们没有那么强大的力量。

sentences.en: Other countries often try to prevent this.
sentences.zh: 其他国家通常会试图防止这种情况发生。

sentences.en: For example, in the UK and Canada, independent commissions, independent groups draw districts based on census data to make them fairer.
sentences.zh: 例如，在英国和加拿大，独立的委员会、独立的团体根据人口普查数据来划分选区，以使其更加公平。

sentences.en: The US is quite unique, really, as it lets politicians vote for these decisions themselves.
sentences.zh: 美国其实相当独特，因为它让政治人物自己投票决定这些事情。

sentences.en: And of course, politicians are selfish and naturally going to try and secure their party’s power.
sentences.zh: 当然，政治人物是自私的，自然会试图巩固他们政党的权力。

sentences.en: Other countries use proportional representation.
sentences.zh: 其他国家采用比例代表制。

sentences.en: So proportional representation is where seats are given based on overall votes, making gerrymandering less effective.
sentences.zh: 所以比例代表制是指根据总得票率来分配席位，这使得gerrymandering的效果大打折扣。

sentences.en: Gerrymandering is legal in the United States, but I think it raises important questions about fairness and democracy.
sentences.zh: Gerrymandering在美国是合法的，但我认为这引发了关于公平和民主的重要问题。

sentences.en: On the one hand, the US Constitution gives states the power to draw their own congressional districts.
sentences.zh: 一方面，美国宪法赋予各州划分自己国会选区的权力。

sentences.en: And in 2019, the US Supreme Court ruled that courts cannot stop gerrymandering.
sentences.zh: 在2019年，美国最高法院裁定法院不能阻止gerrymandering。

sentences.en: This means that under the law, States are free to draw electoral maps that favor one party.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在法律之下，各州可以自由绘制有利于某一政党的选举地图。

sentences.en: Supporters argue that gerrymandering is simply a part of politics and that every party has the opportunity to use it when they are in power.
sentences.zh: 支持者辩称，gerrymandering只是政治的一部分，每个政党在当权时都有机会使用它。

sentences.en: On the other hand, I personally think gerrymandering can undermine democracy.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我个人认为gerrymandering会破坏民主。

sentences.en: When districts are drawn to benefit one party, whether the Democrats or the Republican Party, politicians are essentially choosing their voters, instead of the voters choosing their representatives.
sentences.zh: 当选区的划分是为了让某一个政党（无论是民主党还是共和党）受益时，政治人物实际上是在挑选他们的选民，而不是由选民来选择代表。

sentences.en: It can make elections less competitive and reduce the influence of groups of voters, especially minority voters, even if they make up a significant part of the population.
sentences.zh: 这会降低选举的竞争激烈程度，并削弱特定选民群体（尤其是少数族裔选民）的影响力，即使他们占了人口相当大的比例。

sentences.en: There are some legal limits in the USA. The Voting Rights Act protects minority voting power and tries to prevent districts from being drawn in ways that weaken minority votes.
sentences.zh: 美国有一些法律限制。《选举权法》保护少数族裔的投票权，并试图防止以削弱少数族裔选票的方式来划分选区。

sentences.en: And some states, like I think California, use nonpartisan, groups of people who are not politically aligned, to draw their districts and try and reduce the influence of party politics.
sentences.zh: 而且一些州，比如我想加利福尼亚州，会使用无党派的团体——也就是没有政治站位的人——来划分选区，试图减少党派政治的影响。

sentences.en: I guess my question for all of you listening is, Should this be allowed?
sentences.zh: 我想我抛给各位听众的问题是：这应该被允许吗？

sentences.en: Should gerrymandering be allowed? But before we get to the end of the episode, there are many other interesting political terms in English.
sentences.zh: 应该允许gerrymandering吗？但在我们结束本期节目之前，英语里还有许多其他有趣的政治术语。

sentences.en: Gerrymandering is one of my favorite. In fact, it’s one of my favorite English words.
sentences.zh: Gerrymandering是我的最爱之一。事实上，它是我最喜欢的英语单词之一。

sentences.en: When I studied political science at high school and university, I really enjoyed learning the more unique political terms and concepts.
sentences.zh: 当我在高中和大学学习政治学时，我真的很喜欢学习那些更独特的政治术语和概念。

sentences.en: So I thought I would end this episode by introducing a few more.
sentences.zh: 所以我想在这期节目结束时再介绍几个。

sentences.en: A few more interesting English political words.
sentences.zh: 几个更有趣的英语政治词汇。

sentences.en: Let’s start with filibuster. A filibuster is a tactic in politics where a politician speaks for a long time to delay or block a vote.
sentences.zh: 让我们从“冗长辩论”（filibuster）开始。Filibuster是政治上的一种策略，即政治人物发表很长时间的演讲来拖延或阻止投票。

sentences.en: This is often used in parliaments and congresses, when a party wants to stop a law from passing.
sentences.zh: 这经常用于议会和国会，当一个政党想要阻止一项法律通过时。

sentences.en: For example, in 1957 Strom Thurmond spoke for 24 hours and 18 minutes in the US Senate.
sentences.zh: 例如，在1957年，Strom Thurmond在美国参议院发表了长达24小时18分钟的演讲。

sentences.en: He was attempting to stop the US government from introducing civil rights for African Americans.
sentences.zh: 他试图阻止美国政府为非裔美国人引入民权。

sentences.en: He wasn’t the nicest politician. But he recited the entire US Bill of Rights, the Declaration of Independence, and many other historical documents.
sentences.zh: 他可不是什么最好的政治人物。但他背诵了整部美国《权利法案》、《独立宣言》以及许多其他历史文件。

sentences.en: Another interesting term is pork barrel.
sentences.zh: 另一个有趣的术语是“猪肉桶”（pork barrel）。

sentences.en: Pork barrel refers to government spending on local projects designed to please voters or legislators.
sentences.zh: 猪肉桶是指政府对地方项目的支出，旨在取悦选民或议员。

sentences.en: For example, a politician might fund a new bridge in their district to gain support from local residents.
sentences.zh: 例如，一个政治人物可能会资助他们选区的一座新桥，以获得当地居民的支持。

sentences.en: There was an example of pork barrel politics or pork barreling in the London area of Tower Hamlets a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 几年前，在伦敦陶尔哈姆莱茨（Tower Hamlets）地区，就有一个关于猪肉桶政治或搞猪肉桶项目的例子。

sentences.en: The mayor of the area used a lot of his budget to give things to the Bangladeshi community living in Tower Hamlets.
sentences.zh: 该地区的市长动用了他很大一部分预算，来给住在陶尔哈姆莱茨的孟加拉国社群发放福利。

sentences.en: They were his biggest supporters, but only made up about 30% of the population.
sentences.zh: 他们是他最大的支持者，但只占人口的30%左右。

sentences.en: However, he won elections based on the votes of those 30% of people.
sentences.zh: 然而，他凭借这30%的人的选票赢得了选举。

sentences.en: The other 70% did not receive much funding from his mayoral office.
sentences.zh: 剩下的70%并没有从他的市长办公室获得多少资金。

sentences.en: A lame duck is not a bird that can’t fly, but a lame duck is an elected official whose power is weakened because they will soon leave office.
sentences.zh: “跛脚鸭”（lame duck）可不是指不会飞的鸟，而是一位权力被削弱的民选官员，因为他们即将离任。

sentences.en: For instance, a president in the final months of their term might be called a lame duck because Congress and the public pay less attention to their decisions.
sentences.zh: 例如，处于任期最后几个月的总统可能会被称为跛脚鸭，因为国会和公众对他们的决策关注度会下降。

sentences.en: A QUANGO is a quasi autonomous, non-governmental organization, or QUANGO.
sentences.zh: QUANGO是一个准自治非政府组织（quasi autonomous, non-governmental organization）的缩写，也就是QUANGO。

sentences.en: Which is a very long term, but it basically means it’s funded by the government, but operates independently.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很长的术语，但它基本上意味着它由政府资助，但独立运作。

sentences.en: Quangos often manage public services without direct political control.
sentences.zh: Quango经常在没有直接政治控制的情况下管理公共服务。

sentences.en: These were a big, big news topic in the UK when I was in high school, I think so in the 2010s, and many of them were shut down.
sentences.zh: 在我读高中时，也就是2010年代左右，这些在英国是大得不得了的新闻话题，其中许多后来都被关停了。

sentences.en: A Whip is a political party official whose job is to make sure members vote according to party lines.
sentences.zh: “党鞭”（Whip）是一个政党官员，其职责是确保党内成员按照党派路线投票。

sentences.en: Whips communicate between leaders and members trying to keep everyone in agreement.
sentences.zh: 党鞭在领导层和成员之间进行沟通，试图让每个人达成一致。

sentences.en: These are often found in countries with parliamentary democracies like the UK, Australia, Canada, and India.
sentences.zh: 这些职位常见于实行议会民主制的国家，如英国、澳大利亚、加拿大和印度。

sentences.en: And then finally, the final interesting political word I’ll introduce today, is horse trading.
sentences.zh: 最后，我要介绍的最后一个有趣的政治词汇是“幕后交易”（horse trading）。

sentences.en: Horse trading refers to negotiating and making political deals.
sentences.zh: Horse trading指的是谈判和达成政治交易。

sentences.en: Often involving compromise or backroom arrangements.
sentences.zh: 通常涉及妥协或幕后安排。

sentences.en: Politicians might trade support on one bill to gain votes for another.​
sentences.zh: 政治人物可能会通过在一项法案上给予支持，来换取对另一项法案的选票支持。​

sentences.en: Today I talked about gerrymandering. What it is, why it happens, and how it affects politics in the United States.
sentences.zh: 今天我聊了gerrymandering。它是什么、为什么会发生，以及它是如何影响美国政治的。

sentences.en: We looked at the current situation in Texas and some other US states and then explored some unusual political terms.
sentences.zh: 我们审视了得克萨斯州和美国其他一些州的现状，然后探讨了一些不寻常的政治术语。

sentences.en: Gerrymandering shows how political power can be shaped, not just by votes, but also by the way districts are drawn.
sentences.zh: Gerrymandering表明了政治权力是如何被塑造的，不仅通过选票，还通过选区的划分方式。

sentences.en: While it is legal in the USA, it raises questions about fairness and democracy.
sentences.zh: 虽然它在美国是合法的，但它引发了关于公平和民主的问题。

sentences.en: The choice between political advantage and fair representation is something that every voter and every citizen of a country should think about.
sentences.zh: 在政治利益和公平代表之间做出选择，是每个选民和每个国家的公民都应该思考的事情。

sentences.en: Understanding terms like filibuster, pork barrel, lame duck, QUANGO, whip, horse trading, and of course, gerrymandering can also help you follow political news and conversations more easily.
sentences.zh: 理解诸如filibuster、pork barrel、lame duck、QUANGO、whip、horse trading，当然还有gerrymandering这样的术语，也能帮助你更轻松地关注政治新闻和对话。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Do you think gerrymandering is fair or should it be banned?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你认为gerrymandering是公平的，还是应该被禁止？

sentences.en: And which of the political terms that I discussed today did you find the most interesting or useful?
sentences.zh: 在我今天讨论的政治术语中，你觉得哪一个最有趣或最有用？
